```{r step 1, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# 2024-ONLY POLITICAL ATTITUDES
#
# Outcomes:
#   aiworry   = worry that AI will take respondent's job
#   bizmoney  = belief that business leaders make money
#               at the expense of ordinary people
#   lkelyvot  = likelihood of voting in 2024
#
# Model progression:
#   1. Employment status
#   2. Employment status + social class
#   3. Employment status + JQI
#   4. Employment status + social class + JQI
#   5. Full model: + prestige + income
#
# All analyses restricted to 2024.
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Packages
# ------------------------------------------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(MASS)
library(broom)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Restrict to 2024 and construct outcomes
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_2024 <- jqi_political %>%
  filter(year == 2024) %>%
  mutate(

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # AI worry
    #
    # Original:
    # 1 = very worried
    # 2 = somewhat worried
    # 3 = neither
    # 4 = not very worried
    # 5 = not at all worried
    #
    # Reverse so higher = MORE worried
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    aiworry_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(aiworry)
    ),

    aiworry = case_when(
      aiworry_num %in% 1:5 ~ 6 - aiworry_num,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    aiworry = ordered(
      aiworry,
      levels = 1:5
    ),


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Business leaders
    #
    # Original:
    # 1 = strongly agree
    # 2 = agree
    # 3 = neither
    # 4 = disagree
    # 5 = strongly disagree
    #
    # Reverse so higher = MORE agreement
    # that business leaders make money at
    # the expense of ordinary people.
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    bizmoney_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(bizmoney)
    ),

    bizmoney = case_when(
      bizmoney_num %in% 1:5 ~ 6 - bizmoney_num,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    bizmoney = ordered(
      bizmoney,
      levels = 1:5
    ),


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Likelihood of voting
    #
    # Original:
    # 1 = extremely likely
    # 2 = very likely
    # 3 = somewhat likely
    # 4 = not very likely
    # 5 = not at all likely
    #
    # Reverse so higher = MORE likely to vote.
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    lkelyvot_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(lkelyvot)
    ),

    lkelyvot = case_when(
      lkelyvot_num %in% 1:5 ~ 6 - lkelyvot_num,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    lkelyvot = ordered(
      lkelyvot,
      levels = 1:5
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Check 2024 outcome distributions
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_2024 %>%
  summarise(
    aiworry_n = sum(!is.na(aiworry)),
    bizmoney_n = sum(!is.na(bizmoney)),
    lkelyvot_n = sum(!is.na(lkelyvot))
  )


table(
  jqi_2024$aiworry,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

table(
  jqi_2024$bizmoney,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

table(
  jqi_2024$lkelyvot,
  useNA = "ifany"
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Pooled model-comparison function
# ------------------------------------------------------------

run_2024_model_comparison <- function(
  data,
  outcome
) {

  # Variables needed by the full model
  vars_needed <- c(
    outcome,
    "wrkstat_factor",
    "social_class_factor",
    "compensation",
    "benefits",
    "earnings_stability",
    "prestige",
    "log_realrinc"
  )

  # Common complete-case sample
  model_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::select(
      dplyr::all_of(vars_needed)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na() %>%
    droplevels()

  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Model formulas
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  f1 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor"
    )
  )

  f2 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor"
    )
  )

  f3 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor + ",
      "compensation + benefits + earnings_stability"
    )
  )

  f4 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor + ",
      "compensation + benefits + earnings_stability"
    )
  )

  f5 <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor + ",
      "prestige + compensation + benefits + ",
      "earnings_stability + log_realrinc"
    )
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Fit models
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  m1 <- MASS::polr(
    f1,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  m2 <- MASS::polr(
    f2,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  m3 <- MASS::polr(
    f3,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  m4 <- MASS::polr(
    f4,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  m5 <- MASS::polr(
    f5,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # LR tests
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  lr_m1_m2 <- 2 * (
    as.numeric(logLik(m2)) -
      as.numeric(logLik(m1))
  )

  lr_m1_m3 <- 2 * (
    as.numeric(logLik(m3)) -
      as.numeric(logLik(m1))
  )

  lr_m2_m4 <- 2 * (
    as.numeric(logLik(m4)) -
      as.numeric(logLik(m2))
  )

  lr_m4_m5 <- 2 * (
    as.numeric(logLik(m5)) -
      as.numeric(logLik(m4))
  )


  # Degrees of freedom
  df_m1_m2 <-
    attr(logLik(m2), "df") -
    attr(logLik(m1), "df")

  df_m1_m3 <-
    attr(logLik(m3), "df") -
    attr(logLik(m1), "df")

  df_m2_m4 <-
    attr(logLik(m4), "df") -
    attr(logLik(m2), "df")

  df_m4_m5 <-
    attr(logLik(m5), "df") -
    attr(logLik(m4), "df")


  # ----------------------------------------------------------
  # Return everything
  # ----------------------------------------------------------

  list(

    outcome = outcome,

    n = nrow(model_data),

    models = list(
      "1. Employment status" = m1,
      "2. Employment status + social class" = m2,
      "3. Employment status + JQI" = m3,
      "4. Employment status + social class + JQI" = m4,
      "5. Full model" = m5
    ),

    lr_tests = tibble::tibble(

      outcome = outcome,

      comparison = c(
        "M1 vs M2: Social class beyond employment status",
        "M1 vs M3: JQI beyond employment status",
        "M2 vs M4: JQI beyond employment status + social class",
        "M4 vs M5: Prestige + income beyond employment status + social class + JQI"
      ),

      lr_statistic = c(
        lr_m1_m2,
        lr_m1_m3,
        lr_m2_m4,
        lr_m4_m5
      ),

      df = c(
        df_m1_m2,
        df_m1_m3,
        df_m2_m4,
        df_m4_m5
      ),

      p_value = c(
        pchisq(
          lr_m1_m2,
          df = df_m1_m2,
          lower.tail = FALSE
        ),
        pchisq(
          lr_m1_m3,
          df = df_m1_m3,
          lower.tail = FALSE
        ),
        pchisq(
          lr_m2_m4,
          df = df_m2_m4,
          lower.tail = FALSE
        ),
        pchisq(
          lr_m4_m5,
          df = df_m4_m5,
          lower.tail = FALSE
        )
      )
    ),

    fit = tibble::tibble(

      outcome = outcome,

      model = c(
        "1. Employment status",
        "2. Employment status + social class",
        "3. Employment status + JQI",
        "4. Employment status + social class + JQI",
        "5. Full model"
      ),

      n = nrow(model_data),

      logLik = c(
        as.numeric(logLik(m1)),
        as.numeric(logLik(m2)),
        as.numeric(logLik(m3)),
        as.numeric(logLik(m4)),
        as.numeric(logLik(m5))
      ),

      AIC = c(
        AIC(m1),
        AIC(m2),
        AIC(m3),
        AIC(m4),
        AIC(m5)
      ),

      BIC = c(
        BIC(m1),
        BIC(m2),
        BIC(m3),
        BIC(m4),
        BIC(m5)
      ),

      df = c(
        attr(logLik(m1), "df"),
        attr(logLik(m2), "df"),
        attr(logLik(m3), "df"),
        attr(logLik(m4), "df"),
        attr(logLik(m5), "df")
      )
    )
  )
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Run all three outcomes
# ------------------------------------------------------------

outcomes_2024 <- c(
  "aiworry",
  "bizmoney",
  "lkelyvot"
)

models_2024 <- purrr::map(
  outcomes_2024,
  ~ run_2024_model_comparison(
    data = jqi_2024,
    outcome = .x
  )
)

names(models_2024) <- outcomes_2024


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. LR tests
# ------------------------------------------------------------

lr_tests_2024 <- purrr::map_dfr(
  models_2024,
  ~ .x$lr_tests
)

print(lr_tests_2024)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Model fit table
# ------------------------------------------------------------

fit_2024 <- purrr::map_dfr(
  models_2024,
  ~ .x$fit
)

print(fit_2024)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Extract JQI coefficients from Models 3–5
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_coefficients_2024 <- purrr::map_dfr(
  models_2024,
  function(result) {

    purrr::map_dfr(
      result$models[
        c(
          "3. Employment status + JQI",
          "4. Employment status + social class + JQI",
          "5. Full model"
        )
      ],
      function(model) {

        broom::tidy(model) %>%
          dplyr::filter(
            term %in% c(
              "compensation",
              "benefits",
              "earnings_stability",
              "prestige",
              "log_realrinc"
            )
          ) %>%
          dplyr::mutate(
            statistic = estimate / std.error,
            p.value = 2 * pnorm(
              abs(statistic),
              lower.tail = FALSE
            )
          )
      },
      .id = "model"
    ) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        outcome = result$outcome
      )
  }
)

jqi_coefficients_2024


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Compact Model 4 table
# ------------------------------------------------------------

model4_coefficients_2024 <- jqi_coefficients_2024 %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    model == "4. Employment status + social class + JQI"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    term,
    estimate,
    std.error,
    statistic,
    p.value
  )

model4_coefficients_2024



# ============================================================
# 2024 DEMOGRAPHIC PREDICTORS OF POLITICAL ATTITUDES
# ============================================================

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Check the variables currently available
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_2024 %>%
  dplyr::select(
    aiworry,
    bizmoney,
    lkelyvot,
    age,
    sex,
    racecen1,
    educ,
    log_realrinc,
    wrkstat_factor,
    social_class_factor
  ) %>%
  summary()


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Make sure demographic variables are appropriately coded
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Make demographic variables explicit
# ------------------------------------------------------------

jqi_2024 <- jqi_2024 %>%
  mutate(

    # Age
    age_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(age)),

    # Education
    educ_num = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(educ)),

    # Income
    log_realrinc = as.numeric(log_realrinc),

    # Sex
    sex_factor = case_when(
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sex)) == 1 ~ "Male",
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(sex)) == 2 ~ "Female",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    sex_factor = factor(
      sex_factor,
      levels = c("Male", "Female")
    ),

    # Race: retain White and Black only
    race_group = case_when(
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(racecen1)) == 1 ~ "White",
      suppressWarnings(as.numeric(racecen1)) == 2 ~ "Black",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),

    race_group = factor(
      race_group,
      levels = c("White", "Black")
    ),

    # Employment status
    wrkstat_factor = factor(wrkstat_factor),

    # Subjective class
    # "No class" has already been excluded by making it NA
    social_class_factor = factor(
      social_class_factor,
      levels = c(
        "Lower class",
        "Working class",
        "Middle class",
        "Upper class"
      )
    )
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Verify
# ------------------------------------------------------------

table(
  jqi_2024$race_group,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

table(
  jqi_2024$sex_factor,
  useNA = "ifany"
)

table(
  jqi_2024$social_class_factor,
  useNA = "ifany"
)



# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Function for demographic-only ordered logit models
# ------------------------------------------------------------

run_2024_demographic_model <- function(
  data,
  outcome
) {

  vars_needed <- c(
    outcome,
    "age_num",
    "sex_factor",
    "race_group",
    "educ_num",
    "log_realrinc",
    "wrkstat_factor",
    "social_class_factor"
  )

  model_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::select(
      dplyr::all_of(vars_needed)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::drop_na() %>%
    droplevels()

  formula_demographic <- as.formula(
    paste0(
      outcome,
      " ~ age_num + sex_factor + race_group + ",
      "educ_num + log_realrinc + ",
      "wrkstat_factor + social_class_factor"
    )
  )

  model <- MASS::polr(
    formula_demographic,
    data = model_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )

  coefs <- as.data.frame(summary(model)$coefficients)

  coefs$term <- rownames(coefs)
  rownames(coefs) <- NULL

  names(coefs) <- c(
    "estimate",
    "std.error",
    "statistic",
    "term"
  )

  coefs <- coefs %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      p.value = 2 * pnorm(
        abs(statistic),
        lower.tail = FALSE
      ),
      outcome = outcome,
      n = nrow(model_data)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      outcome,
      term,
      estimate,
      std.error,
      statistic,
      p.value,
      n
    )

  list(
    outcome = outcome,
    n = nrow(model_data),
    model = model,
    coefficients = coefs
  )
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Run models for all three outcomes
# ------------------------------------------------------------

outcomes_2024_demo <- c(
  "aiworry",
  "bizmoney",
  "lkelyvot"
)

demographic_models_2024 <- purrr::map(
  outcomes_2024_demo,
  ~ run_2024_demographic_model(
    data = jqi_2024,
    outcome = .x
  )
)

names(demographic_models_2024) <- outcomes_2024_demo


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Extract coefficient tables
# ------------------------------------------------------------

demographic_coefficients_2024 <- purrr::map_dfr(
  demographic_models_2024,
  ~ .x$coefficients
)

demographic_coefficients_2024
